Warn about a problem in one group-time cell

Source: R/pte.R
pte_cell_warning.Rd

For use inside an attgt_fun. Signals a warning that compute.pte() (and so pte()) collects across group-time cells instead of issuing one warning per cell. After the loop over cells, it gives one warning per distinct summary, listing each affected cell (with the group and period in the original coding of gname and tname) and its detail. Warnings are reported for the original sample only, not again for each empirical bootstrap draw.

Called outside compute.pte(), it is an ordinary warning with message "<summary>: <detail>". The condition has class "pte_cell_warning".

Usage

pte_cell_warning(summary, detail)

Arguments

summary

one line describing the kind of problem. Cells with the same summary are reported together, so it should not depend on the cell.

detail

what happened in this cell, e.g. a share of treated units or the names of covariates.

Value

Called for its side effect (a warning); returns NULL invisibly when the warning is muffled.

Examples

my_attgt <- function(gt_data, ...) {
  n_treated <- sum(gt_data$D[gt_data$name == "post"])
  if (n_treated < 50) {
    pte_cell_warning("Few treated units", paste(n_treated, "treated units"))
  }
  pte_attgt(gt_data, xformula = ~1, d_outcome = TRUE)
}
if (requireNamespace("did", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # one warning, listing the cells of the 2004 and 2006 cohorts
  res <- pte(
    yname = "lemp", gname = "first.treat", tname = "year",
    idname = "countyreal", data = did::mpdta, setup_pte_fun = setup_pte,
    subset_fun = two_by_two_subset, attgt_fun = my_attgt, biters = 0
  )
}
#> Warning: Few treated units (8 cells):
#>   group 2004, period 2004: 20 treated units
#>   group 2006, period 2004: 40 treated units
#>   group 2004, period 2005: 20 treated units
#>   group 2006, period 2005: 40 treated units
#>   group 2004, period 2006: 20 treated units
#>   group 2006, period 2006: 40 treated units
#>   group 2004, period 2007: 20 treated units
#>   group 2006, period 2007: 40 treated units
